description:
## Why

The crate's RevocationFetcher trait is meant to be pluggable, but consumers want to drop in a working backend. `ureq` is the right reference choice for the sync path:
- pure Rust (no openssl-sys / native-tls C dep complexity)
- small dep tree (vs reqwest blocking which pulls tokio runtime + hyper)
- MSRV-friendly
- straightforward HTTP/1.1 GET/POST API

## What

Feature-gated module `pkix_revocation_http::clients::ureq`:

```toml
[features]
client-ureq = ["dep:ureq"]
[dependencies]
ureq = { version = "...", optional = true, default-features = false, features = ["tls"] }  # exact featureset TBD
```

```rust
#[cfg(feature = "client-ureq")]
pub struct UreqFetcher {
    agent: ureq::Agent,
    max_response_size: usize,    // default 10 MiB
}

#[cfg(feature = "client-ureq")]
impl UreqFetcher {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn with_agent(agent: ureq::Agent) -> Self;
    pub fn with_max_response_size(self, n: usize) -> Self;
}

#[cfg(feature = "client-ureq")]
impl RevocationFetcher for UreqFetcher {
    fn fetch(&self, req: &FetchRequest) -> Result<FetchResponse, FetchError> {
        // Translate FetchRequest -> ureq::Request, set Content-Type for POST,
        // bound response read with max_response_size, return bytes.
    }
}
```

Map ureq errors to FetchError variants:
- network/transport: FetchError::Transport(Box::new(err))
- non-2xx: FetchError::HttpStatus(status)
- response body exceeded max_response_size: FetchError::TooLarge

## Acceptance

- [ ] UreqFetcher works with both GET (CRL) and POST (OCSP).
- [ ] Content-Type header set on POST requests.
- [ ] Response size bounded; exceeding triggers TooLarge.
- [ ] Status code 200 -> Ok; non-2xx -> Err(HttpStatus).
- [ ] Mock-server integration test (PKIX-a1yc.9) uses this.
- [ ] No `unsafe`. ureq's TLS featureset chosen to avoid C deps if possible.

## Out of scope

- Async (PKIX-a1yc.10).
- HTTP/2 (rare in OCSP/CRL deployments; not blocking).
- Custom proxy / cert-pinning configuration (consumer can pass a pre-built ureq::Agent).

## Effort

~120 lines + tests.
